title: The Four Wars: The Discrete Stages of Divine Operation against Self-Love
arc: The teaching narrates four successive wars waged by the Sons of Light against the Sons of Darkness, each fought by a distinct divine emanation — First Man, Living Spirit, Third Ambassador, and Jesus the Radiance — and read together they describe the four discrete stages by which the Lord conquers the proprium and gathers the captive Living Soul home to its vessel of light.
reading:
This teaching presents the cosmic drama of redemption as four successive wars between the Sons of Light and the Sons of Darkness. The four wars are not four repetitions of the same conflict but four discrete operations of the Divine, each handling self-love at a different degree and each accomplishing what the previous stage made possible. Read together, they trace the whole arc by which Divine Truth descends into the proprium, structures what it has subdued, reveals itself within the structured state, and finally glorifies the human so that the Living Soul can ascend.

The **first war** is that of the First Living Man — Divine Truth descending into the realm of self-love. He goes down against the King of Darkness and his archons, binds the five worlds of self-love, and plants what is called "his tree, which is the Living Soul." This is the initial seeding of Divine Truth into the natural mind. The teaching says these planted truths lie "hidden within in the manner of fish" — Divine Truth submerged in the receptive depth of the natural, not yet visible, but really sown. At the same time the First Man "cuts down and tears up the roots" of the bitter tree, the corrupt perception that grows from Hyle. So the first war does two things at once: it implants the seed of regeneration and severs the root of the false perception. This is the descent itself, the engagement that makes everything subsequent possible.

The **second war** is that of the Living Spirit. Where the First Man descended, the Living Spirit now structures. He binds the archons "in the midst" of the lands and confines them in three strongholds — the confirmed binding-state in which the powers of falsity are held against breaking out. The archons recoil, set themselves against him, and recognize that he intends to bind them. But the Living Spirit operates "in many faces, in many multitudes, in many guises, in great single-mindednesses": that is, the structuring Divine accommodates itself in countless forms of order, so that no falsity can escape his hand. This is the work of regeneration in its building register — divine wisdom imposing form, ordering the natural, fixing the boundaries within which the captive light can begin to be sorted.

The **third war** is that of the Third Ambassador. Now that the proprium is bound and structured, what is required is the revealing call. The Ambassador displays "his image" — the icon of Divine Truth — toward the lower side, where all the light and "wealth" of the captives are stored. The teaching gives a vivid picture of how this image works: a man comes "being mighty," richly clothed in silver and luxurious adornment, and the entire archonic host, in their boasting, is "likened" to him. They imagine themselves rich, they walk as rich men — and in that very moment of being drawn upward toward the seductive likeness, they are purified and cleansed. This is the operation of the Lord's revealed image extracting good from the mingled state: by displaying the true icon to the proprium, the proprium aspires upward, releases its hidden light, and is cleansed of it.

The **fourth war** is that of Jesus the Radiance. With the proprium bound (war one), structured (war two), and emptied of its captive light (war three), the final stage is the glorification of the human and the consummation of the whole work. Jesus the Radiance comes down upon the entire archonic host of upper and lower side, "strips" them, and "establishes the whole structure." This is the stripping away of the foul garment and the building of the New Man. He humbles the archons in a "great battle" and "carries out the purpose of heart of the Greatness" — the inmost will of the Father is fulfilled in ultimates. The result is "the hope of Adam," the redemption of the natural man, brought "unto his vessel of light." The closing fragments name "the counsel" and "the Call and the Answer," confirming that this fourth stage is the consummation of conjunction: the soul has heard, has answered, has been gathered into its vessel.

The teaching ends by pointing past the four wars toward the final state, where Death is overthrown, kingship is established "for ages of ages," and "every elect" comes to dwell in the likeness of the Five (the five-fold Living Soul restored), under the King who shall raise them. The four wars are thus the complete process of regeneration read as cosmic history: descent, structure, revelation, glorification. They are also the four discrete degrees of how the Lord acts within any soul that is being regenerated — first by sowing truth into the natural like fish hidden in water, then by ordering and binding the falsities, then by displaying the icon that calls captive light upward, and finally by stripping the old man and building the new in its vessel of light. Each war is necessary; none can be skipped; together they are the single redemptive movement by which the Living Soul comes home.
